verdict.rationale: Corporations Canada names delegated-access roles in its own docs: a "full access manager" or "filing collaborator" can file, otherwise a corporation key is needed, and there is a "Manage shared access and permissions" page. Registered intermediaries are also mentioned. But the pack does not show what each role may or may not do. missing for 10: published authorization forms, a role-by-role permission matrix, which signatures or attestations stay personal to directors or officers, and any independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: you must already have access as a full access manager or filing collaborator. Otherwise, you will need a corporation key. Manage shared access and permissions
(if you are a registered intermediary) It will cost $200 and will take 1 day.
